title: Personal Portfolio v2.0
shortDescription: A next-generation personal portfolio website featuring a fully interactive terminal interface, command-line navigation, dynamic JSON-driven content, and a premium dark aesthetic — built entirely with HTML, CSS, and Vanilla JavaScript.
overview: Personal Portfolio v2.0 is a complete rebuild of Akash Prajapati's personal portfolio website — designed to stand out with a unique interactive terminal experience at its core. Unlike conventional portfolio sites, this version features a fully functional terminal command-line interface where visitors can explore projects, skills, certifications, and contact information through typed commands. The entire site is data-driven — all content (profile, projects, skills, certifications, education) is sourced from individual JSON files, enabling easy updates without touching the codebase. The design follows a premium dark-mode aesthetic with glassmorphism, gradient accents, and smooth animations throughout. The terminal supports custom commands, help menus, autocomplete, and animated output responses.
features: Interactive terminal interface with custom command-line navigation
Command history, autocomplete, and help menu in the terminal
JSON-driven content architecture — all data loaded dynamically from JSON files
Separate JSON files for profile, skills, projects (micro + production), certifications, education, and socials
Production project cards with detailed modal overlays
Skills visualization with categorized tech stacks
About me section with personality and tech philosophy
Dark-mode premium aesthetic with glassmorphism and gradients
Custom CSS animation system for smooth transitions
Responsive layout across all device sizes
DataService layer for centralized JSON data fetching
TerminalCommands.js for modular terminal command handling

dataLayer: JSON files (profile, projects, skills, certifications, education)

architecture.pattern: Single Page Application with JSON Data Layer
architecture.description: A vanilla HTML/CSS/JS single-page application where all content is loaded dynamically from a structured set of JSON data files. The JavaScript layer is organized into services (DataService for data fetching) and components (terminal, project cards, sections) for maintainability.
dataFiles: data/projects-production/ — individual JSON files per production project

myRole: Sole Developer. Designed and built the entire portfolio from scratch — including the terminal interface, JSON data architecture, DataService layer, component system, CSS design system, and all content.
challenges: Building a fully functional terminal interface in pure Vanilla JavaScript with command history, autocomplete, and formatted output rendering
Designing a JSON-driven architecture where all content is decoupled from the codebase — enabling easy updates across dozens of data points
Creating a unique, memorable portfolio experience that stands out from typical portfolio websites while remaining professional and navigable
Managing the state and rendering of the DataService to efficiently load and cache JSON data across multiple UI sections
Designing and implementing detailed production project JSON schemas that are comprehensive enough for rich modal rendering yet simple enough to maintain
solutions: Built a dedicated TerminalCommands.js module that maps command strings to handler functions — with a base command parser that supports arguments, flags, and multi-line formatted output
Implemented a DataService singleton that fetches all JSON files once on load and caches them in memory, exposing methods for individual section data retrieval
Designed the terminal experience as the central UX differentiator — a feature-first approach that makes the portfolio inherently interactive and exploratory
Used Promise.all for parallel JSON file loading during initialization, then exposed individual getter methods on the DataService for lazy section rendering

Created a consistent JSON schema across all production project files with required fields (id, title, overview, features, techStack, images) and optional enrichment fields (architecture, challenges, solutions)
keyLearnings: Building a terminal emulator in Vanilla JavaScript — command parsing, history management, and formatted rich-text output
JSON-driven content architecture for portfolios — separating data from presentation for maintainability
DataService design patterns in Vanilla JavaScript — singleton pattern, async data fetching, and caching strategies
Advanced CSS techniques for premium dark-mode aesthetics — glassmorphism, gradient layering, and animation systems
Modular JavaScript component architecture without a framework — organizing code into services and component handlers

colorPalette.theme: Premium Dark Mode with gradient accents
